Anya: Heads-up — I see a perf regression in the block-grain kernel selector on MQA models when paged KV is enabled. p99 token/sec drops ~25% on long sequences.
Sam: Oof. Can you repro locally or is this in staging?
Anya: Repro in staging small cluster (2xA100). Happened after the stripe allocator change yesterday.
Ricardo: Do you have a minimal repro workload? sequence lengths, batch sizes, and whether KV page size changed?
Anya: Minimal: opt-qa-mqa-30b, seqs=2048/4096 mixes, batch=4 (microbatching on), kv_page=256KB, block_grain=64. Saw stable drop across runs.
Sam: Can you paste the perf regression snippet?
Anya: Sure — here's wallclock from the inference runner for the same prompt: ```
baseline: 78.4 tokens/s (old picker)
current: 58.9 tokens/s (block-grain selector v2)
p99 latency: 240ms -> 360ms
cpu%/gpu% roughly same
```
Ricardo: Interesting. That smells like increased kernel launch/fragmentation overhead for paged KV when block_grain is small. Could be bad memory coalescing.
Lu: My theory: the allocator's stripe alignment now yields more partial stripes per KV page which forces kernels into a narrow vector length path (extra branches). On MQA we already have more head packing, so combined effect amplifies.
Sam: Worth trying two quick experiments: 1) bump block_grain to 256 to see if coalescing improves; 2) force stripe-aware kernel (fallback) to check if selector mis-ranked the kernel.
Anya: Running both now on staging. Test harness: ```
./run_perf --model opt-qa-mqa-30b --seq-mix "2048:0.6,4096:0.4" --batch 4 --kv-page 256 --block-grain 256
./run_perf --model ... --kernel-policy stripe-aware
```
perf-bot: Alert: kernel-selector-score deviation detected for opt-qa-mqa-30b at 2290001200. Score delta: -0.31 vs baseline. See /logs/2290001200 for trace. :warning:
Ricardo: Also capture NVPROF/Nsight minimal trace for the slow run — I'm curious about SM occupancy and L2 traffic. Small kernels with bad occupancy show this pattern.
Anya: Attached nvprof snippet (cropped): ```
Time(%)  Kernel                 Calls  Avg ms
45.3     paged_attn_block64     120    0.42
30.1     kv_prefetch_stripe     240    0.18
12.2     kernel_dispatch_small  480    0.09
```
Lu: paged_attn_block64 dominating — that block size might be in a bad code path for these sequence lengths. Our selector probably ranked it higher because of microbatch latency predictions but actual prefetch miss pattern kills throughput.
Sam: If bumping block_grain fixes it, then we need a quick autotune rule: when kv_page >= 256KB and avg_seq > 1024 prefer block_grain >= 128 for MQA. Also add a perf test to the CI regression suite.
Anya: Results: block_grain=256 -> 76.2 tokens/s; stripe-aware kernel -> 74.9 tokens/s. Both close to baseline. So hypothesis confirmed.
Ricardo: Good. Action items: (1) add a selector feature for kv_page and seq_distribution (Sam), (2) add an autotune sweep that runs stripe-aware vs block-grain choices across common kv_page sizes (Ricardo), (3) revert allocator patch if we see more wide regressions (Lu/infra).
Sam: I'll file a short RFC and add the quick autotune job to nightly. Also add a short canary rollout pin for the selector change so Dedicated customers don't hit this.
Anya: Filing ticket now: INF-3627. Pinned logs: /ops/infra/INF-3627/context and perf traces at /traces/2290001200.
perf-bot: Note: scheduled nightly autotune run added (INF-3627) :white_check_mark:
Ricardo: Thanks — let's monitor the next deploy. If anyone sees similar in other MQA sizes, @Sam @Lu please ping.
Sam: Will do. Thanks team :thumbsup:
